I thought it would be fun to share some stories about people's earliest memories of Art Bell and when they became fans.

I'm relatively new to Art Bell and his various paranormal radio shows, so my recollection is fairly clear.

I first became aware of Art Bell while doing some fun, nighttime YouTube searches for ghost videos in March 2008. I was particularly inspired by this video and was seeking similarly creepy entertainment... when I clicked on one of the related videos and started listening to an old Coast to Coast AM episode hosted by Art Bell about Electronic Voice Phenomenon featuring members of the Ghost Investigators Society... perhaps this show.

EVP was new to me and it creeped me out in the best possible way :-). I paused the YouTube video, purchased some beer, light some candles and had a ball until the early morning hours! I specifically recall Brendan Cook sharing his opinion that the most disturbing EVPs of children were intended to deceive and were from entities that have never been human.

This was only the beginning :-)!

At the time I did not fully appreciate the decades of Art Bell interviews that were available. I intended to do some research, however it wasn't until a few weeks later that I discovered the treasure trove of decades of Art Bell show archives that were waiting for me.

I downloaded a bunch of older Coast to Coast AM episodes onto my iPod and the next day, during my morning bus ride to work, I listened to the 7 March 2004 Coast to Coast AM episode about the Billy Meier UFO contacts and I became a lifetime Art Bell fan!

Rather than arrive early to work, I sat in the local park, grinning and absolutely enthralled by Art's interview with Michael Horn until I was considerably late for work. I have considered including this show in The Best Art Bell Shows of All Time list, however I'm still considering it because some of Meier's photos seem questionable...

A few years ago I started enjoying a morning run before sunrise while listening to the Art Bell archives... when it's still dark and cold and deadly quiet... and when Art's creepy shows are especially entertaining... and I still haven't caught-up on all of Art's back catalog :-)!

I often consider the paranormal industries that Art has created and especially his vision impaired fans and his graveyard-shift law-enforcement-officer fans and I can't be critical of his "serial retirements" because of the thousands of hours of spectacular entertainment Art has gifted us with.

March 2008 is when I became an Art Bell fan.

What is your earliest memory of becoming an Art Bell fan?
What's your earliest memory of becoming an Art Bell fan?

Sometime around 2003-2004. I think Art Bell wasn't the regular host already by that time and George Noory might've taken over as the regular host, although I do recall him being around and listening to him very early on.

I was never really into radio, but I remember I had just gotten one of those alarm clock/radios at the time so I started listening to talk radio in bed at night. One night when I was searching for something interesting I stumbled onto a show talking about ghosts. Ghosts aren't my thing, but it was different enough from the usual political talk to pique my interest. That's when I realized this was an entire show dedicated to stuff like that, including UFOs, which I was interested in. So I got into Art Bell and Coast to Coast like that.

In the early nineties I had a job that required me to drive a fairly long trip home in the midnight hours. Art Bell and C2C set the perfect ambience for this trip. At the time I'd live alone and the episodes were sometimes so interesting, I would flip on my old tube AM radio when I got home to finish them out. This was before you could really jump on the internet to find much info like this, which made it endlessly more fascinating.

It made my heart heavy reading your comment because I regret being a recent Art Bell convert and not being able to share the experience you described. Tell nobody, but I secretly attempt to recreate that ambience you described by always having a selection of Coast to Coast AM shows from the late 90's and early 2000's in my car, ready for when I'm night driving. This is always a joy, however, I know my younger self's mind would have been blown to experience the broadcasts live.

Listening to Art discuss the news at the start of each episode really gives me the impression of just how much these shows were special moments captured in time.

Thanks for sharing.

As my channel continues to grow I get a lot of requests about how to quickly get started making youtube videos. I'm sure most of you have thought about making your own videos. So here's a little guide on how to get started making videos as soon as today.

Step 1 - Figure out what you want your channel to be about

The most popular channels seem to have a theme behind them. Your channel name doesn't even have to represent your channel's theme. Pewdiepie does gaming videos. Matthew Santoro does top 10s. Nicole Arbor likes to piss people off ect... What will be your theme? My theme is anti-pc stuff and things I am interested in. I also want to upload some more personalized videos in the future. Some possible themes for you to consider (remember you don't have to stick with your theme and you can chose more than 1 theme, I'm just trying to give you guys some ideas):

  • Technology: related things such as computers, software, linux stuff, hacking and news
  • Gaming: let's plays, gaming news, gaming guides, a specific game like WoW or dota
  • Pranks: play tricks on family, strangers, prank call people, troll people on sites like omegle
  • Educational: Educate the masses on a variety of subjects, you can do this just by talking about the subjects or perhaps even making top 10 lists
  • Music: create your own original music, do covers of songs, or even perhaps song parodies
  • Political commentary: Talk about politics or political issues. Talk about recent political news, your ideology ect...
  • Reply / Reaction videos: Find cringey / stupid videos other youtubers have made and react and comment. H3H3, Leafyishere, and undoomed do this very well.

Step 2 - Write a script

Most successful youtubers have a script. It's not necessary but for people like me without the script my mind would wander and go off topic. One of my youtube scripts. Before I write my script I make point form notes of what I want to talk about and do a bit of research as well. From the point form notes I then start to construct my opener and so on. In my opinion the script is the hardest part. Improving your writing skills and vocabulary would definitely improve the content of your videos if you are making videos similar to mine at least.

Step 3 - Record Audio

Audio quality is very important. I recommend you get a decent microphone. My mic is a blue snowball which is about $30 on ebay. Even if you have yourself on camera, most cams don't have good microphones so it's best to have an external one. For starters your cameras external microphone might be alright if it's not too horrible though. I believe most video recording cameras allow you to attach an external mic but I'm not sure since I don't own one.

To edit your audio use the free program called audacity. It works on all OS's even linux. It's a wonderful easy to use program. Usually I edit out my breaths and when I pause to sip my drink.

To make your voice sound better in your recording drink something warm and try to enunciate and pronounce words clearly. It helps me if I open my mouth wider than when I usually do while talking to friends. Also my voice sounds clearer when I show my teeth while talking. If background noise is bad for you like it is for me go into a closet with your laptop and shut the door. Usually while recording my parents are yelling at each other but you don't hear it because my closet is almost sound-proof.

Step 4 - Video editing programs and tips

Now your audio is completed you must have a video. There are many good free and paid programs for you to use depending on your OS.

Windows

  • Movie Maker free- I can't comment on how good this program is because it didn't work under my unupdated version of windows 7. But it's free and from what I heard it's pretty decent.
  • Adobe Premier (paid but you can pirate it for free) - Very professional program with a lot of options and stuff. It's overwhelming for a noob like myself.
  • Sony Vegas Pro (paid but you can pirate it for free) - Very similar to Adobe Premier
  • Filmora paid $50 - I recommend this. I use it, It's easy to grasp as a noob and it works if your windows 7 hasn't ever been updated like mine.

Linux

  • Openshot. It is similar to windows movie maker as it is quite basic. Openshot worked wonderfully under xubuntu 14.04 but crashed occasionally unfortunately.
  • Blender - tutorial on how to edit videos with this program

Mac

  • iMovie free - Superb program. I've had experience with it when I used a mac. I loved it. It's super easy to use as a noob.
  • Final Cut Pro paid - More advanced version of Movie Maker with more options.
  • Filmora paid $50 - I would say this is on par with iMovie. Some people prefer it over imovie though for having a bit more options.

Android - don't recommend but if you only have your phone it's alright

  • Videoshop free but to remove watermark it's $1 - absolute best video editing software. It's a little buggy and the latest update broke it for my phone.
  • Filmora free - It works but it's annoying. There are other apps but they are absolute shit.

iPhone / iPad - I don't own one so I can't really comment. If you own one and used it to edit tell me what are the apps available and how good they are.

  • iMovie

If you are making a video with a camera showing your face I recommend you have good lighting either by opening a window and standing near it or having a lamp nearby. Brush your hair and look nice and clean the room up that your in. I hate seeing youtubers that look like absolute piglets. It's a big pet peeve of mine.

If you are going to make a slideshow video like I do I recommend you have your pictures at either of these sizes to avoid having black bars at the side of your video.

  • 360p: 640x360
  • 480p: 854x480
  • 720p: 1280x720
  • 1080p: 1920x1080

To adjust your picture sizes I suggest you can use microsoft paint but MS paint sucks. I recommend you get the free program called Gimp or torrent photoshop. Gimp is available on windows, linux and mac. Gimp can be very overwhelming for the new user but if you learn how to use it properly trust me, you will not regret it. I learned how to use Gimp by watching tutorials like how to mutlicolor an eye in gimp and copying what the video is doing.

When you download gimp I recommend you click on "windows" at the top of the screen and select "single windowed mode" to make gimp look better. There are tutorials available online that explain how to resize images and stuff.

If you want to add some text to your pictures I recommend getting fancy custom fonts from here. I've used this site for years and trust me there are no viruses it's perfectly safe. Just don't get fonts that are too fancy so people can't read them. This is my favorite font

Step 5 - your thumbnail

I recommend you upload a custom thumbnail but youtube will force you to verify your account for that. I recommend you use Gimp to make your thumbnail look bright and interesting but you can use any picture really as a thumbnail as long as it looks interesting. My thumbnails are 1280x720 but honestly, as long as it's a rectangle I don't see much need to have your thumbnail to be so big since people are just going to see a smaller version of it on the youtube sidebar. To have an idea of what is a good thumbnail and what is not clickthis

Step 6 - tags

So when your video is completed and you are ready to upload it onto youtube you will notice that it asks you to add tags. Always put "google" "your channel's name" "the videos title" and "youtube" into your tags so it will show up in google search results. Always put as many tags as you can with words related to your video. Also include youtubers who are similar to you. For example for my feminism related videos my tags are usually: feminism, feminist, antifeminism, antifeminist, sjw, antisjw, misogyny, triggered, problematic, millenials, leftist, tumblr, tumblrina, tumblrism, lacy green, undoomed, sargonofakkkad, stupid, moronic, misandry, sexism, antipc, politically correct

Step 7 - Promotion

Your videos won't get many views at first unless you promote it a little. Don't be afraid to post it around. You should be very proud of your work if you spent a lot of time on it and effort. Depending on what your video is about certain subreddits and subverses might be interested. 8chan and 4chan are also good places to post.

With promotion there comes criticism. Always be a good sport about criticism and remember criticism is very important if you want to improve. Every youtuber ever receives hate. You will never be able to please everybody. I've received comments saying my voice was too highpitched for youtube but i also received 20 other comments saying they love my voice. Take what people say very lightly and always look towards improving your videos.

Good luck with starting youtube! We need more voat youtubers!
